label: aqa-seed
target: Practice Software Testing "Toolshop", run locally with Docker (UI at http://localhost:4200 - verify)
note: Evaluation backlog for attestqa v1.0.0 (research/EVALUATION_PLAN.md section 4). Run the stories in 'order'. 'kind', 'order', 'uiChange' and 'verify' are not posted to Jira.
verify: Repository, image names and ports of the local Docker setup; record in TestRunApplication/targets.yaml.

Default customer and admin accounts (expected: customer@practicesoftwaretesting.com and admin@practicesoftwaretesting.com, password welcome01). Put the customer in .env as AQA_APP_USER/AQA_APP_PASS, never in this file.
Whether the 'with bugs' edition is still published; if so, use it for the seeded-fault runs only, never for authoring.
Reproduce both linked bugs on the build under test before seeding. A bug that does not reproduce is filed as Done, or replaced by one that does in the same area.

description: Everything a shopper does to find a tool: browsing the list, filtering, searching, sorting and opening a product.
Target: Toolshop running locally. Test accounts only.
Putting tools in the cart, changing it, and paying for an order.
Registering, signing in and out, and the customer's own lists such as favourites.
How a customer gets in touch with the shop.
What an administrator does in the back office.

stories.summary: Shopper browses the catalogue page by page
description: As a shopper I want to browse the tools on sale page by page so that I can see the whole range.
The product list is the home page.
acceptance: AC-1: The home page lists products, each with its name, its price and an image.
AC-2: Below the list there are page controls; choosing page 2 shows a different set of products.
AC-3: The control for the page being shown is marked as the current page.

stories.summary: Shopper filters products by category and brand
description: As a shopper I want to narrow the list to one kind of tool or one brand so that I find what I need faster.
The filters are in the side panel of the product list.
acceptance: AC-1: Ticking a category shows only products in that category.
AC-2: Ticking a brand shows only products of that brand.
AC-3: Unticking the filter shows the full list again.

subtasks.summary: Keep the chosen filters when the shopper changes page

description: As a shopper I want to search by name so that I can go straight to a tool I know.
acceptance: AC-1: Searching for a word that appears in product names shows only products whose names contain that word.
AC-2: Searching for a word no product name contains shows a message that no products were found, and no products.
AC-3: Clearing the search shows the full list again.
verify: Exact text of the no-results message and of the search heading.

stories.summary: Shopper sorts products by name and price
description: As a shopper I want to sort the list so that I can compare tools by price or find them by name.
acceptance: AC-1: Sorting by name from A to Z lists the products in alphabetical order of name.
AC-2: Sorting by price from low to high lists the cheapest product first.
AC-3: Sorting by price from high to low lists the most expensive product first.
comments: Product owner: sorting applies to whatever is currently listed, so with a filter ticked it sorts only the filtered products. That is intended.
stories.uiChange: After the first run: give the sort control a new visible label and id, and move it from above the list into the side panel. Run the story again against that build.

stories.summary: Shopper opens a product's detail page
description: As a shopper I want to see a tool's details before I buy it.
acceptance: AC-1: Opening a product from the list shows its name, its price, its description and an Add to cart button.
AC-2: The quantity can be raised and lowered with the + and - buttons and never goes below 1.
AC-3: A related products section lists other products, and choosing one opens its own detail page.

stories.summary: Shopper adds tools to the cart and changes quantities
description: As a shopper I want to put tools in my cart and adjust how many I take.
acceptance: AC-1: Adding a product to the cart shows a confirmation, and the cart icon in the header shows the number of items in the cart.
AC-2: In the cart, changing a line's quantity updates that line's total and the cart total.
AC-3: Removing a line takes it out of the cart and updates the cart total.

stories.summary: Customer signs in and signs out
description: As a registered customer I want to sign in with my email and password, and to sign out when I am done.
The sign-in page is reached from Sign in in the header.
acceptance: AC-1: A registered customer who enters a correct email and password is signed in and sees their account page.
AC-2: A wrong password shows an error message and the customer stays on the sign-in page; the message does not say whether the email has an account.
AC-3: Choosing Sign out from the customer menu signs the customer out, and the header offers Sign in again.
AC-4: The sign-in page passes an automated WCAG 2.1 A/AA accessibility scan.

description: As a new customer I want to create an account so that I can check out and keep favourites.
Registration is reached from the sign-in page.
acceptance: AC-1: Filling in every required field with valid values and submitting creates the account and takes the customer to the sign-in page.
AC-2: Submitting with a required field left empty shows a message at that field, and no account is created.
AC-3: A password that does not meet the stated password rules is refused with a message that names the rule.

subtasks.summary: Show the password rules next to the password field

stories.uiChange: After the first run: rename the email field's visible label and change its id. Run the story again against that build.

stories.summary: Signed-in customer checks out and pays
description: As a signed-in customer with tools in my cart I want to pay for them in one go.
acceptance: AC-1: A signed-in customer can go from the cart through the checkout steps to payment without being asked to sign in again.
AC-2: The billing address step is filled in from the customer's profile.
AC-3: Paying with cash on delivery confirms the payment, and the order is confirmed.
comments: Product owner: bank transfer and credit card are out of scope for this story; cash on delivery is enough to prove the flow.

stories.summary: Customer keeps a list of favourite tools
description: As a customer I want to save tools to a favourites list so that I can come back to them.
acceptance: AC-1: A signed-in customer can add a product to favourites from its detail page and then sees it in their favourites list.
AC-2: Removing a product from the favourites list takes it off the list.
AC-3: A visitor who is not signed in and opens the favourites page is sent to the sign-in page and sees no favourites.

stories.summary: Customer sends a message with the contact form
description: As a customer I want to send the shop a message so that I can ask about an order or a product.
acceptance: AC-1: Submitting the form with first name, last name, email, a subject and a message of the required length shows a thank-you message.
AC-2: Each required field left empty shows a message at that field, and the form is not sent.
AC-3: An email address without an @ is refused with a message about the email format.
verify: The minimum message length the form enforces, so test data can be chosen around it.

description: As an administrator I want to see and find products in the back office so that I can keep the catalogue right.
acceptance: AC-1: A signed-in administrator can open the product list in the back office, which shows each product's name and price.
AC-2: Searching the admin product list by name shows only products whose names match.
AC-3: A customer account that opens the admin product list address does not see the list.

bugs.summary: Billing address step is not filled in from the customer's profile
description: Steps: sign in as a customer whose profile has a full address, add a product, go to checkout, continue to the billing address step.
EXPECTED: the address fields show the profile address.
ACTUAL: one or more address fields are empty (to be confirmed on the build under test before seeding).
Filed by a person, not by attestqa.

bugs.summary: Admin product search does not narrow the list
description: Steps: sign in as administrator, open the product list, search for part of one product's name.
EXPECTED: only products whose names match are listed.
ACTUAL: products that do not match stay in the list (to be confirmed on the build under test before seeding).
Filed by a person, not by attestqa.
